title: Ar-Rafi', the Exalter
hookLine: the Exalter, who raises the humble
tomorrow: unveiling night. who's missing from the thank-you list?

cards: A shout-out in someone else's post can carry a person for a week. Yesterday's question: Amira gets one sentence in the caption, so who does she lift?
She picks Luis, the barista who came in early to prime the wall and never asked to be in a picture. One question for today, then: who gets raised, and by whom?

teach.b: Islam's answer is a name: ar-Rafi', the Exalter, who raises the humble. In the traditional list it stands right beside yesterday's al-Khafid.

In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase: charity never shrinks wealth, forgiving only adds to a person's honor, and no one humbles themselves for Allah's sake except that Allah raises them.
And the Qur'an names who goes up, in Pickthall's words: "Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks." Now a neighbor who says it in her own words.
In the Hebrew Bible, Hannah has prayed for a child, and when her son is born she sings.
In her song, in the book of Samuel, the Lord makes poor and makes rich, brings low and lifts up, and raises the poor out of the dust to sit among princes.

What the two share: the One who lowers the proud is the same One who lifts the low, and people don't hand out the real raising, God does. And an honest difference: Hannah sings about God's acts, as thanks for a son.
In Islam, the Exalter is also a name, one of the names a believer calls on directly, beside its partner, the Abaser.
Two ways of saying it, and one thing for a friend tonight: in both, the lifting starts at ground level, from the dust.

how: Muslims learn al-Khafid and ar-Rafi' as a pair, and the hadith that humbling yourself for Allah's sake brings raising is taught alongside them.

o: the One who lifts the dead back to life
the One who rewards the most successful
the One who raises up the humble

games.q: who gets raised — tap the pairs.
p: lifts the poor out of the dust

s: humbling yourself means you'll always stay at the bottom
the hadith says the opposite: no one humbles themselves for Allah's sake except that Allah raises them.
Hannah's song in the book of Samuel speaks of God lifting the poor from the dust
brings low and lifts up, and seats the poor among princes.
Hannah's song and the Islamic names say exactly the same thing in the same way
they share the lowering and lifting; Hannah sings of God's acts, while Islam also calls on ar-Rafi' as a name.

games.q: a classmate who never speaks up gives the best answer in a group project. the group is about to present. what fits today's lesson?
o: make sure she presents her part, by name.
present it yourself; it's smoother if the confident one talks.
leave it; real humility means she wouldn't want credit.
games.why: the raising is God's, but people can stop standing in its way. naming the quiet one is lifting someone up.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose work usually goes unseen: a cook, a janitor, a coworker who does the boring part well. Write them a short message, just what they did and that it mattered, and use the sit to get the words right.
Sending it is up to you.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Rafi': the Exalter, who raises the humble, from the dust and to high ranks. The partner of al-Khafid.

orig.note: Arabic: the Exalter, who raises. beside al-Khafid, the Abaser, in the traditional list.

carryVoice: Hold this one: he raises, and the humble are the ones he lifts. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2588 (charity doesn't decrease wealth; forgiving adds honor; humbling oneself for Allah brings raising)

sources.q: Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks.
